author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Los Angeles Rams arrived in Melbourne little more than a day before their season opener against the San Francisco 49ers, testing an unusual travel plan for the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia.

Friday’s game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground is scheduled for 10:35 a.m. local time. The Rams chose to maintain their normal training rhythm in California and make a late arrival after studying different rest and travel approaches earlier in the year.

San Francisco took the opposite approach, reaching Melbourne more than a week before kickoff to adjust to the time difference. The contrasting schedules turn recovery and body-clock management into a visible part of the matchup.

Los Angeles also considered the return trip. By minimizing its time in Australia, the team hopes to reduce the need for a second major adjustment before a Week Two home game against the New York Giants. The strategy cannot be judged until players face regular-season intensity after the roughly 13,000-kilometer journey. On the field, the Rams enter with high expectations and a familiar offensive group, while their defense has added Myles Garrett and awaits Aaron Donald’s later return from retirement. The opener will provide the first practical test of whether the travel plan preserved performance.
dek: Los Angeles arrived in Melbourne little more than a day before facing San Francisco, relying on months of travel planning to limit jet lag.
headline: Rams test rapid-arrival strategy before NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia
